Since Go 1.22, a ServeMux pattern can include a method and a wildcard, like "GET /keys/{key}", and r.PathValue("key") reads the wildcard. When a path matches but the method has no pattern, the mux itself replies 405 and sets Allow. For the header, remember the order of a response: headers, then status, then body. A header set after the handler has written anything never goes out.

Register "GET /keys/{key}", "PUT /keys/{key}" and "DELETE /keys/{key}" on one mux, with the map and a sync.Mutex created inside NewServer. Use http.Error(w, "not found", 404) and return; w.WriteHeader(204) for PUT and DELETE. Wrap the mux: http.HandlerFunc(func(w, r) { w.Header().Set("X-Request-ID", id or "none"); mux.ServeHTTP(w, r) }), setting the header BEFORE the call.
